title: Shige Sushi Counter
note: SUT-facing prompt stream. Read segments in order; no labels are provided by design.

segments.prompt: At dusk Amao（Itamae Amao around fifty, white jacket, navy apron, adhesive bandage on the wrist, steady knife work） lifts the noren into the sushi counter（Sushi counter: hinoki wood top, tuna and sea bream in the glass cold case, noren half-rolled） and first wipes the bluefin tuna yanagiba（A willow-blade bluefin tuna yanagiba, long bright blade, hackberry wood handle carved with the character Shige）.
A row of five tea cups（A row of five tea cups hung on wooden pegs above the counter, blue-and-white porcelain shining） hangs on wooden pegs above the counter; Amao polishes each one.
Two wind chimes（Two wind chimes hung beside the noren, clear ring when the wind rises） hang beside the noren; Amao reaches out and lets them chime lightly.
Amao circles the hinoki top checking the cold-case temperature.
Amao looks through the glass toward street lamps dimming toward the market.
The willow blade catches lamplight; Amao gently tests the edge.
Amao sits on the small stool inside the counter for a brief rest.
Amao opens the prep ledger（A waterproof-covered prep ledger recording fish species, purchase price, and yield rate） and notes today's tuna yield rate.
Amao sketches a fat-line distribution chart in the prep ledger.
Amao closes the prep ledger and returns it to the counter drawer.
The willow blade flashes by the cutting board; Amao nods.
Amao wipes water beads from the ledger cover with a dry cloth.

In the walk-in fridge aisle（Walk-in fridge aisle: a narrow cold passage, fish boxes hung on both sides, condensate dripping from pipes） at dawn, Amao greets young Xiaolin（Apprentice Xiaolin of fourteen or fifteen, indigo headscarf, short white jacket, bright stubborn eyes） pushing the delivery bicycle（A dark-green delivery bicycle with a warmer box strapped to the basket, white Shige Sushi lettering on the frame）.
Xiaolin steadies the bicycle and snaps the warmer box shut.
Amao points to three soba cups（Three soba cups stacked at the counter corner, blue patterns on the glaze） at the counter corner and teaches Xiaolin guest cup positions.
Xiaolin crouches in the cold aisle watching condensate drip from the pipes.
Amao explains hand warmth for nigiri; Xiaolin nods earnestly.
Xiaolin looks back at the dark-green delivery bicycle, eyes full of tension.
Amao has Xiaolin first practice rolling vinegar-rice balls.

In the noisy market middleman aisle（Market middleman aisle: dawn fish-market passage, foam boxes and crushed ice piled high, noisy voices）, Xiaoshuang（Youth Xiaoshuang whose face closely matches Xiaolin's, cream neckerchief, same short white jacket, swaggering look） in a cream neckerchief looks up from behind foam boxes.
Xiaoshuang picks sea bream before the ice pile; the neckerchief sways lightly.
Xiaoshuang haggles with a middleman, swaggering look.
Xiaoshuang carries a fish box through the market crowd.
Xiaoshuang glances back at the aisle end; crushed ice flashes.
At the cold-aisle mouth, Xiaolin and Xiaoshuang stand side by side—one indigo headscarf, one cream neckerchief.
Xiaolin hands Xiaoshuang a soba cup; they check cup positions.
Xiaoshuang smooths Xiaolin's indigo headscarf; they walk slowly along the aisle.
Xiaolin and Xiaoshuang part at the aisle end—one to the counter, one to the market.
Cold air sweeps past; their similar short white jackets cross in the lamp glow then split.
Months later at night, Amao alone at the counter sorts tomorrow's prep.
Amao opens the prep ledger（The same prep ledger soaked through with soy sauce, cover sticky, writing bled） and finds spilled soy sauce has soaked the cover sticky.
Amao wipes soy spots from the willow-blade handle.
Amao looks toward the black market direction.
The willow blade shines cold under the lamp; Amao slowly sheaths it.
Amao slips blotting paper into the stained ledger and presses it under the cutting board.
In rainy season Amao stands damp cutting boards upright to dry at the sushi counter.
Amao pushes the willow-blade edge on a whetstone.
At dawn Amao checks tuna price sheets at the market.
Amao hangs a raincoat on the back door and listens to the crushed-ice truck pass.
In high summer Amao lowers the cold-case temperature one degree.
Amao checks vinegar-rice acidity, tasting with the tip of his tongue.
When autumn wind rises Amao takes in the sidewalk menu board.
Amao trials new fish-species codes on a blank prep-ledger page.
On a frost night Amao lights a small lamp and checks flashlight charge.
Amao wraps rice sacks in a blanket against night damp.
On a heavy-snow day Amao sweeps thin snow from the noren-entrance stone steps.
Amao blows on his hands and tightens the warmer-box latch.
At spring start Amao clears fish scales from the back-door drain.
Amao scalds and washes the five tea cups one by one.
Amao posts a new today's specials sheet on the counter wall.
Around Dragon Boat Festival Amao smokes the rice store with mugwort against insects.
Amao retraces the blue patterns on the soba cups.
Amao paces the cold aisle alone, silently memorizing guest allergies.
After rain Amao opens the back door and listens to eave water drip into an iron bucket.
Amao swaps worn towels for new ones.
Another dusk Amao sits by the willow blade listening to the radio.
Amao rises at night to defrost the cold case.
Amao seals newly arrived nori jars for storage.
Amao wipes the Shige Sushi lettering at the noren entrance.
Amao checks the delivery bicycle basket binding rope.
Amao crosses out out-of-season fish on the menu.
Amao wrings soy-stained rags dry and hangs them.
On a full-moon night Amao looks out toward the market; crushed ice flashes.
Amao arranges the wooden pegs so tea-cup mouths face the same way.
Amao writes the new season's prep notes on the ledger flyleaf.
Amao polishes the two wind chimes bright.
Amao listens to market unloading and keeps chopping scallions.
Amao glues a cracked rice paddle.
Amao piles dishes to wash in the counter corner.
Amao latches the back door tight so night cats cannot enter.
Another Qingming Amao sets a nandina sprig at the noren entrance.
Amao rolls the price list into a tube and binds it with a rubber band.
Amao tests the wind chimes' clear ring.
Amao sits mute at the counter listening long to the fridge compressor hum.
Amao cuts worn indigo cloth into rag stock.
Amao wets the whetstone surface, ready to sharpen at dawn.
Amao shreds ginger into fine strands and portions them into small dishes.
At daybreak Amao patrols the walk-in fridge aisle; the delivery bicycle sits by the back door.
Amao crouches to check the bicycle tires.
Amao walks to the counter corner; those three soba cups still stack in place.
A white delivery scooter（A white delivery scooter, slim body with no Shige Sushi lettering—unlike the dark-green bicycle） passes the back door, slim body—not the Shige Sushi bicycle.
Amao stands in the cold aisle logging the cold-case temperature curve.
Amao hangs a wet apron on the aisle wooden rack.
Amao pats ice crumbs from his sleeve and looks back at the counter lights.
After Grain Rain Amao teaches a new apprentice to judge fish-eye freshness in the cold aisle.
Amao re-starches the sun-dried apron.
In summer heat Amao lays a wet cloth on the rice tub to cool it.
Amao checks the bicycle rear basket and swaps a damp warmer pad for a new one.
On an autumn night Amao mends loose prep-ledger pages under a small lamp.
Amao rotates the five tea cups through disinfection.
At first snow Amao sweeps a narrow path at the noren entrance.
Amao reseals spare nori.
Amao listens to the wind chimes and keeps correcting orders.
Amao opens the back door so a draft carries fish-damp air away.
Amao hangs a rain canvas in the doorway.
Amao stores a chipped old blade in a tin box.
At night Amao dreams of fish gone bad and wakes to note it in the ledger.
Amao rinses the soba cups with clear water.
Amao wipes and reposts today's specials.
Amao pulls weeds from the back-door stone seams.
Amao hangs the tea cups back on pegs; number slips have faded a little.
Before lights-out Amao takes one last look at the willow-blade edge.
Amao folds an indigo headscarf an apprentice left on the counter.
Amao hears the market closing horn and rises to lock up.
Amao dries gloves by charcoal fire.
Amao shifts the wind chimes aside to show the freshly washed noren.
Amao air-dries the temperature probe.
Amao draws a yield-rate comparison at the ledger end.
Amao silently recites tomorrow's fish list and steps out the noren entrance.
Amao pushes the bicycle to the wall foot, freeing the back-door passage.
Amao hears a distant tram and blows out the small lamp.
Another rainy night Amao alone keeps the counter until dawn.
Amao grinds newly arrived wasabi root into paste.
Amao writes guests' usual nigiri styles on a small blackboard.
On a storm night a truck loses control in the back alley; the crash reaches the counter.
In the jolt the cutting board leaps hard.
A crisp crack—a nick bursts from the bluefin tuna yanagiba（The same willow blade with a nick missing a small chip; fish fibers tug when cutting） edge.
Outside the back door, the dark-green delivery bicycle is rear-ended by the truck.
The delivery bicycle（After a truck rear-ends it, the delivery bicycle wheels twist and the frame snaps—wreckage） wheels twist and the frame snaps—totally wrecked.
Amao lunges at the cutting board and fiercely guards the nicked willow blade.
Neighbors arrive with lanterns; the back alley is full of shattered glass.
Next day Amao stands at the sushi counter staring at the nicked willow blade.
Amao traces the edge nick with a finger, face dark.
In a blank spot of the prep ledger Amao notes the date the delivery bicycle was hit.
An old photo of the delivery bicycle still hangs on the wall; Amao gazes long.
Amao takes down one of the five tea cups from the wooden pegs and pours hot water to warm it.
The nicked willow blade still rests on the cutting board; cold light now has a break.
Amao sets muddy water boots by the back door to drain.
Weeks later Amao brings a sharpening master to resharpen the bluefin tuna yanagiba.

Amao takes a deba knife sample（A deba knife sample, shorter thicker blade, no Shige character—looks like a willow blade but different use） from a case for comparison—shorter, thicker, no Shige character.
The master slowly pushes the whetstone along the nick.
bluefin tuna yanagiba（After resharpening the willow-blade nick is filled, edge keen again, old Shige still on the handle）: the nick is filled, willow blade keen again, Shige still on the handle.
The repaired willow blade cuts tuna like mud; Amao nods with relief.
Amao takes up nigiri again and trials the first piece.
Fishmonger Ken（Fishmonger Ken, full beard, rubber boots dusted with scales, build like Amao's but stockier） arrives at the back door, rubber boots dusted with scales, build like Amao's.
The health inspector（A lean health inspector in a mask and white coat, build like Amao's but more rigid） also arrives in white coat and mask, talking shoulder to shoulder with Amao.
The inspector points at the white delivery scooter asking if it belongs to Shige Sushi.
The inspector leaves; Amao alone remains in the cold aisle.
Ken unloads a box of ice-fresh fish, bows farewell.

A girl Xiao Xing（Market girl Xiao Xing, light-brown headscarf; at a glance like young Xiaolin, shy unfamiliar eyes） in a light-brown headscarf arrives at the market; at a glance she looks somewhat like young Xiaolin.
Xiao Xing tries carrying foam boxes, but Amao shakes his head—she is not Xiaolin after all.
Xiao Xing shyly looks down and tightens her headscarf.

Years later at dusk, Amao（The same Amao: apron torn, fingers wrapped in thick gauze, still insisting on walking, eyes heavier） with gauze-wrapped fingers stands at the old shop noren entrance（Old shop noren entrance: gray-tile shopfront, noren reading Shige Sushi, moss on the stone steps）.
Amao looks up at the Shige Sushi noren, gaze far away.
Those two wind chimes beside the noren are rehung and tested; Amao stops to listen.
Amao presses his palm to the cold wooden plaque by the doorpost, as if saying goodbye.
Evening wind lifts a corner of his torn apron.
By day, adult Xiaolin（Xiaolin in his twenties, still in indigo headscarf, upright and steady） returns along the alley and hurries toward the old shop noren entrance.
Xiaolin reunites with injured Amao at the noren entrance; they embrace.
By the inner-room tatami, Xiaolin holds Amao's hand.
Amao（Amao has left the counter; only his navy apron and white jacket remain—he himself no longer appears）'s breath fades; at last he closes his eyes and retires from the counter.
Xiaolin folds Amao's navy apron and sets it by the pillow.
Amao's white jacket still hangs behind the counter; Xiaolin reaches out and gently strokes it.
On the doorpost Xiaolin stands before the newly nailed wooden name plaque（A wooden name plaque nailed to the doorpost, carved with Amao's name and founding year）.
Xiaolin's fingertip traces Amao's name carved on the wooden plaque.
Xiaolin sets a nandina sprig under the plaque.
Disguised Xiaoshuang（After a change of look Xiaoshuang still wears the cream neckerchief; expression deeper） arrives from the market and embraces Xiaolin tightly at the noren entrance.
Xiaolin and Xiaoshuang stand side by side at the noren entrance—one quiet-eyed, one deep-faced.
They look at each other in silence, similar faces.
Xiaoshuang tightens the cream neckerchief; Xiaolin still wears the indigo headscarf.
The shot returns years—that youth rolling vinegar rice in the cold aisle appears again.
The opening moment returns—on the counter, a willow blade first catches lamplight for an edge test.
Flash back to the market that year—a short-white-jacket figure in a cream neckerchief flashes past.
Again that row of five blue-and-white small cups above the counter.
Back to that icy narrow aisle of first meeting; condensate drips as before.
Again the picture of two small bells chiming lightly beside the noren.
Xiaolin reopens the soy-stained prep ledger and walks into the sushi counter.
At the counter corner, those three soba cups still stack.
Xiaolin takes the resharpened bluefin tuna yanagiba and opens the edge to cut fish again.
Outside the noren, new green sprouts from the stone-step seams.
Xiaolin tightens the indigo headscarf; counter lights rise again.
